 Mr. Biswajit Manna, Adv.
 ...for the appellant.
 1.
Affidavit-of-service filed in court today be kept on  record.
2. Despite service, none appears for the respondent.
3. The present appeal has been preferred against an order of the Appellate Tribunal affirming the order of the Adjudicating Authority under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
4. Learned senior counsel appearing for the appellant takes several objections to the impugned judgment of the Appellate Tribunal.
5. First, it is argued that the entire premise of the order of the Adjudicating Authority, which was affirmed by the Tribunal, was a purported report of an analyst.

However, the Adjudicating Authority did not attribute any reasons or even arrived at a specific finding as to misbranding, nor discussed the report of the analyst, prior to accepting the same in a perfunctory manner.

6. The Appellate Tribunal, while affirming the said order, supplanted reasons, some of which cited Rules which were beyond the Rules under which the original charges were framed against the present appellant.

7. Learned senior counsel next argues that the statutory guidelines as to awarding penalty were not adhered to or discussed while fixing the quantum of the penalty against the appellant for the alleged misbranding of the appellant's product.

8. It is also argued that although the said Act and the governing Rules and Regulations provide that if the designated officer is of the opinion that a case of misbranding has been made out, he/she has Nestle India Ltd vs Mr. Rupam Mondal on 9 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/20215849/
1 to authorize the Food Safety Officer to file a complaint or application before the Adjudicating Authority.in the present case, such steps were completely bypassed and the designated officer merely issued a note sheet to the Adjudicating Authority de hors the law.
9.
